newsitem.title: USA: Apple CEO says fundamentals top '97 agenda.
newsitem.headline: Apple CEO says fundamentals top '97 agenda.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc Chief Executive Officer Gilbert Amelio said increasing the company's revenue and market share will not be a priority until he can improve Apple's operations and product lines.
The effort may take until 1998, Amelio told investors at the American Electronics Association's Monterey Classic investment conference here.
"I have to have a solid foundation before I can build a castle," he said. Without a solid foundation, he said, Apple would improve its financial results for one or two quarters but could slide again.
Amelio also told the audience Apple is planning an entirely new operating system, the fundamental software that controls the basic functions of a computer, for release in 1998.
The new software system is an attempt to leap-frog Microsoft Corp's competing Windows family of operating systems.
The new operating system will take advantage of much faster computer chips, while reducing the complexity of the software to make computers less prone to crashes, he said.
The company hasn't decided yet whether it will license the new operating system to other makers of personal computers.
"We haven't come to that bridge yet," Amelio said.
